interface.title: distributed-task-queue — Research mode (A task queue whose scheduling policy is an experimental variable)
interface.field: Distributed systems / computer systems performance evaluation (task-queue scheduling policies on Redis Streams)
interface.stage_of_work: Reading and checking published results: looking through finished benchmark results and tracing each claim back to the raw data
interface.what_it_is_for: A one-page interactive results site that compares FIFO, strict priority, EDF and WFQ scheduling across workloads, loads and failure experiments, where every chart can be opened to show its source CSVs, SHA-256 digests, producing command, caveats and underlying numbers.

data.note: All data comes from committed JSON files under /data/*.json, exported from results/*.csv by scripts/export_site_data.py. Opening a figure's dataset link (/data/sweep.json) shows the raw JSON with caveats, command, conditions, manifests and per-run rows. Nothing was uploaded and no backend was contacted. Known site-side inconsistency: in the per-tenant figure under '8 slots · real CPU', the numbers table gives WFQ small/A = 0.015× (9.024 vs 0.133 s, about 68×) while the caption says 39.9×. Neither run checked how the caption figure is calculated, so treat neither value as verified.

tree.general: Judge which work-scheduling policy to trust under which conditions, using benchmark evidence that can be traced to raw data
tree.specific: Compare fifo/priority/edf/wfq on latency, throughput, deadline misses and fairness, read the failover, fencing and partition experiments, and check the report's numbers against source CSVs

features.name: Provenance-wrapped figure

features.specific: Figure component: title + report § tag, caption, '▸ Source:' disclosure (dataset .json link, exporter script, each results/*.csv with row count and sha256 prefix, 'produced by' make/go command, caveats), and '▸ Numbers behind this chart' table that follows the current selection
steps: read the chart and caption
expand Source to see dataset, CSV paths, row counts and sha256
read the 'produced by' command and caveats
expand Numbers behind this chart to read the exact plotted values
open the dataset JSON link to see raw rows

features.specific: Load sweep figure: workload toggle (Uniform/Bursty/Heavy-tailed/Multi-tenant skew) × metric toggle (p99, p50, deadline miss rate, max wait, throughput). Title, caption caveat (heavy-tailed noise), point tooltips and the '(worst − best)/best' spread bars all follow the selection

features.name: Repetition dot-strip with mean bars and a comparability warning
features.general: Show every replicate as a dot with the mean as a bar for each method, switchable by condition and metric. A condition that is not comparable carries a marker on its button and inserts a warning box explaining why
features.specific: Main-matrix figure: workload × 7 metrics. Dots are single 4,000-task experiments, the bar is the mean of 25. Hovering a dot names repetition and run id. Selecting 'Bursty≠' shows the NOT LOAD-MATCHED callout (1.57× vs 1.25×) linking to the load sweep

read the per-policy means and spread of dots
